basic_info: 54-year-old female referred from ER for esophagitis; chief complaint: concern for resolution of prior chest pain
present_illness: Chest pain occurred a few months ago, was sharp and located behind the breastbone in the center of the chest, occurred randomly, did not wake the patient up, lasted four days, could not be relieved, led to ER visit where tests were performed but nothing was found, resolved after three days, no chest pain since then, but had some trouble swallowing at the time. Currently being evaluated for esophagitis. The patient does not currently have symptoms related to esophagitis and has no known family history of cardiovascular disease. The patient does not smoke or drink alcohol and has no typical risk factors for GERD.
past_history: No known family history of cardiovascular disease. No known personal history of smoking or alcohol use.
aux_exam: The patient underwent an EKG and basic blood tests during the ER visit, which were normal. No imaging studies were performed at that time. The patient does not recall the exact names of the blood tests, but they were reported as normal, with no abnormalities detected in cardiac enzymes such as troponin or creatine kinase-MB.
